raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Summary Cooperative TopK groups FP32 scores into coarse bins before selecting candidates. If too many scores land in the bin containing the TopK threshold, its bounded candidate buffer can drop scores that belong in the result. This PR detects that overflow before scattering candidates and uses exact FP32 selection for the affected row. The usual path remains in place when the threshold bin fits. # Context We need to differentiate three things here: * Synthetic vs. real score distributions. * Exact vs. approximate top-K in real NSA/DSA. * The impact of overflow. Even when overflow occurs (which *is a rare event*) the discarded candidates will have the same high bits as the retained ones. Retained and discarded candidates belong to the same current radix-threshold bin. Therefore, they share the radix prefix examined so far, meaning their values are very close. For this reasons, even if we can force the overflow with synthetic inputs, that doesn't mean non-exact topK translates into an negative accuracy impact for the reasons above. See https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53287 for more context. ## Validation and performance I checked selected values against `torch.topk`, along with index range and uniqueness, across ordinary inputs and concentrated-score inputs, including the 2,048/2,049-candidate boundary. B300 CUDA-graph microbenchmarks show that ordinary-input latency is generally close to main. Recovery is not free: at 250K width, 64 rows, and k=2048, a controlled case measured ~40 µs with 2,048 candidates in the threshold bin, ~54 µs with 2,049, ~75 µs when the whole row was concentrated in [1.0, 1.01]. The last case is deliberately extreme and unrealistic; the 2,049 case shows the cost of merely entering recovery. The goal here is an exact TopK result when overflow occurs, not a claimed improvement in model accuracy. Whether the correction changes an evaluation score depends on how often a real workload reaches this condition and how sensitive it is to the selected positions. DeepSelect and Flashinfer topK are now integrated in vLLM and can be selected using `--sparse-indexer-topk-backend deep_select` and `--sparse-indexer-topk-backend flashinfer` respectively. TopK=512 TopK=1024 TopK=2048 Note the [1.0, 1.01] distribution is deliberately extreme and unrealistic, trying to represent worst-case scenario. ### E2E results (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, topk=512) DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash serving runs here show little change in mean TPOT or ITL. Together, these suggest limited practical impact for the workloads tested, but neither experiment measures overflow frequency or rules out an impact on other score distributions. We are including exact selection because the bounded candidate path can potentially drop better scores, while the normal-path overhead is small. Input / output, concurrency | Main TPOT / ITL | Exact cooperative TPOT / ITL | DeepSelect TPOT / ITL -- | -- | -- | -- 512K / 2K, 1 | 4.63 / 4.73 | 4.70 (+1%) / 4.80 (+1%) | 4.95 (+7%) / 5.04 (+6.6%) 256K / 2K, 16 | 7.40 / 8.26 | 7.36 (0%) / 8.36 (+1%) | 7.53 (+2%) / 8.56 (+3.6%) 128K / 2K, 32 | 9.68 / 10.46 | 9.68 (0%) / 10.58 (+1%) | 9.66 (0%) / 10.44 (0%) Results achieved with: `vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash -tp 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 ` and `vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --input-len "$ISL" --output-len 2048 --num-prompts $((c * 4)) --max-concurrency "$c"` ## TODOs - [ ] Extend this to the persistent_topk path - upcomming PR - [ ] Microbenchmarks suggest DeepSelect can be a better topK backend on SM100+, large context lengths, bs>32, and topK=512/1024. This will be studied separatedly in a follow-up PR as well

files.patch:
@@ -1425,6 +1425,140 @@ def test_cooperative_topk_512_tie_workspace_is_per_row() -> None:
     )
 
 
+def _assert_cooperative_topk_exact(
+    logits: torch.Tensor, indices: torch.Tensor, seq_len: int, top_k: int
+) -> None:
+    assert torch.all((indices >= 0) & (indices < seq_len))
+    sorted_indices = indices.sort(dim=1).values
+    assert torch.all(sorted_indices[:, 1:] != sorted_indices[:, :-1])
+    actual = logits.gather(1, indices.long()).sort(dim=1).values
+    expected = logits[:, :seq_len].topk(top_k, dim=1).values.sort(dim=1).values
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not _has_device_capability(90), reason="This test requires SM90+")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("top_k", [512, 1024, 2048])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("seq_len", [8192, 32768, 131072, 262144, 524288])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_cooperative_topk_candidate_overflow(seq_len: int, top_k: int) -> None:
+    row = 1.0 + torch.arange(seq_len, dtype=torch.float32) * (0.01 / seq_len)
+    logits = row.unsqueeze(0).cuda()
+    lengths = torch.tensor([seq_len], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    indices = torch.empty((1, top_k), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+
+    _run_topk_backend("cooperative_topk", logits, lengths, indices, top_k, seq_len)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    _assert_cooperative_topk_exact(logits, indices, seq_len, top_k)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not _has_device_capability(90), reason="This test requires SM90+")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_rows", [9, 34, 64])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("seq_len", [65535, 65536, 65537])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_cooperative_topk_overflow_cluster_boundary(
+    num_rows: int, seq_len: int
+) -> None:
+    top_k = 2048
+    stride = (seq_len + 3) & ~3
+    row = 1.0 + torch.arange(seq_len, dtype=torch.float32) * (0.01 / seq_len)
+    logits = torch.full((num_rows, stride), float("inf"), device="cuda")
+    logits[:, :seq_len] = row.cuda()
+    lengths = torch.full((num_rows,), seq_len, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    indices = torch.empty((num_rows, top_k), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+
+    _run_topk_backend("cooperative_topk", logits, lengths, indices, top_k, seq_len)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    _assert_cooperative_topk_exact(logits, indices, seq_len, top_k)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not _has_device_capability(90), reason="This test requires SM90+")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_rows", [1, 64])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("top_k", [512, 2048])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_cooperative_topk_16bit_grid_overflow(num_rows: int, top_k: int) -> None:
+    seq_len = 32768
+    row = 1.0 + torch.arange(seq_len, dtype=torch.float32) * (0.01 / seq_len)
+    logits = row.to(torch.bfloat16).float().cuda().repeat(num_rows, 1)
+    lengths = torch.full((num_rows,), seq_len, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    indices = torch.empty((num_rows, top_k), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+
+    _run_topk_backend("cooperative_topk", logits, lengths, indices, top_k, seq_len)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    _assert_cooperative_topk_exact(logits, indices, seq_len, top_k)
+
+
+def _negative_halfway_threshold() -> tuple[float, torch.Tensor]:
+    # Top FP32 key of the coarse bin holding -1.0: an FP16 halfway point that
+    # rounds into the bin while the next keys round into the bin above.
+    def coarse_bin(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        bits = x.half().view(torch.int16).to(torch.int32) & 0xFFFF
+        key = torch.where(bits >= 0x8000, ~bits & 0xFFFF, bits | 0x8000)
+        return key >> 6
+
+    one = torch.tensor([-1.0])
+    base = int(one.view(torch.int32))
+    bits = base - torch.arange(0, 1 << 14, dtype=torch.int32)
+    values = bits.view(torch.float32)
+    in_bin = coarse_bin(values) == coarse_bin(one)
+    top = int(in_bin.nonzero().max())
+    near = values[top + 1 : top + 2048]
+    assert bool((coarse_bin(near) == coarse_bin(one) + 1).all())
+    return float(values[top]), near
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not _has_device_capability(90), reason="This test requires SM90+")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("top_k", [512, 1024, 2048])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "num_rows,seq_len", [(1, 262144), (6, 131072), (16, 65536), (64, 65536)]
+)
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_cooperative_topk_overflow_negative_halfway(
+    num_rows: int, seq_len: int, top_k: int
+) -> None:
+    halfway, near = _negative_halfway_threshold()
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seq_len + top_k)
+    num_near, num_needed, num_halfway = 50, 10, 3000
+    num_top = top_k - num_needed - num_near
+    rows = []
+    for _ in range(num_rows):
+        row = torch.full((seq_len,), -100.0)
+        row[:num_top] = 5.0 + torch.rand(num_top, generator=generator)
+        pick = torch.randperm(near.numel(), generator=generator)[:num_near]
+        row[num_top : num_top + num_near] = near[pick]
+        row[num_top + num_near : num_top + num_near + num_halfway] = halfway
+        rows.append(row[torch.randperm(seq_len, generator=generator)])
+    logits = torch.stack(rows).cuda()
+    lengths = torch.full((num_rows,), seq_len, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    indices = torch.full((num_rows, top_k), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+
+    _run_topk_backend("cooperative_topk", logits, lengths, indices, top_k, seq_len)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    _assert_cooperative_topk_exact(logits, indices, seq_len, top_k)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not _has_device_capability(90), reason="This test requires SM90+")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("top_k", [512, 1024, 2048])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_ties,num_needed", [(20, 12), (40, 20), (100, 52)])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_cooperative_topk_negative_inf_ties(
+    num_ties: int, num_needed: int, top_k: int
+) -> None:
+    num_rows = 4
+    seq_len = top_k + num_ties - num_needed
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(num_ties + top_k)
+    logits = torch.full((num_rows, seq_len), float("-inf"))
+    for row in range(num_rows):
+        finite = torch.randperm(seq_len, generator=generator)[: top_k - num_needed]
+        logits[row, finite] = torch.randn(top_k - num_needed, generator=generator)
+    logits = logits.cuda()
+    lengths = torch.full((num_rows,), seq_len, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    indices = torch.full((num_rows, top_k), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+
+    _run_topk_backend("cooperative_topk", logits, lengths, indices, top_k, seq_len)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    _assert_cooperative_topk_exact(logits, indices, seq_len, top_k)
+
+
